stem: The tail of comet is directed away from the Sun, because–

options.label: a
options.text: As the Comet rotates around the Sun, the lighter mass of Comet is pushed away due to centrifugal force alone.

options.label: b
options.text: As the Comet rotates, the lighter mass of the Comet is attracted by some stars situated in the direction of its tail.

options.label: c
options.text: The radiation emitted by the Sun exerts a radial pressure on the comet throwing its tail away from the Sun.

options.label: d
options.text: The Tail of the Comet always exists in the same orientation.

expl: In the outer solar system, comets remain frozen and are extremely difficult or impossible to detect from Earth due to their small size. As a comet approaches the inner solar system, solar radiation causes the volatile material within the comet to vaporize the steam out of the nucleus, carrying the dust away with it. The streams of dust and gas thus released form a huge, extremely tenuous atmosphere around the comet called the coma and the force exerted on the coma by the Sun's radiation pressure causes an enormous tail to form, which points away from the Sun. Hence (c) is the correct answer.

stem: Hale-Bopp is the name of a-
expl: Hale-Bopp is a long period comet that was discovered in 1995. It was shining near the orbit of Jupiter around 23rd July, 1995. This comet was discovered by Alan Hale (New Mexico) and Thomas Bopp (Arizona) so it was named by joining the last names of the two astronomers.

stem: With which planet comet Shoemaker-Levy collide –
expl: Comet Shoemaker-Levy-9 was discovered on 24th March 1993 when astronomers Carolyn Shoemaker, Eugene M. Shoemaker and David Levy captured its glimpse in their Schmidt telescope. During 16-22 July, 1994 it collided with the massive planet Jupiter. In this collision no harm was done to Jupiter. It was the first event of collision, of two components of the solar system seen from the Earth.

options.text: A piece of matter which has entered the earth atmosphere from outer space

expl: A meteor is a bright streak of light in the sky also called a shooting star or a falling star but actually, it is a not a star but it is just a small piece of rock and minerals. It starts glowing because when it enters the Earth’s atmosphere with a very high velocity it burns due to heat caused by air friction. Most of the meteors burn to ashes before reaching the surface of the Earth.
